newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN MINFINS SET RECORDS, TREND UNCLEAR.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN MINFINS SET RECORDS, TREND UNCLEAR.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds set records on Thursday in choppy trade as Wednesday's news about London Club commercial bank creditors' reconcilation process sparked strong short position coverage, dealers said.
They said it was difficult to forecast the trend in the next few days, calling the market overheated, but added they saw no major selling yet.
Traders said short-covering had driven prices up.
However, Natsionalny Rezervny Bank dealer Andrei Ivanov-Golitsyn said: "Now a correction is happening, but we are still higher than yesterday's close."
Bids on all tranches touched new highs though bid/offer spreads widened for many leaving some tranches straddling Wednesday's prices.

Ivanov-Golitsyn said the market had risen on Wednesday's news that Russia had reconciled about 65 percent of its debt to the London Club and saw rescheduling agreements closing by the end of the year.
He estimated turnover involving Russian traders at about $200 million.
A dealer at a major Western bank said he saw no selling.
"No one will give you a forecast now -- we have been expecting profit-taking since yesterday. Maybe, it will happen tomorrow, but no one is selling."
He said the market rose by 0.5 basis points from Wednesday's close.

Ivanov-Golitsyn said spreads on MinFins over U.S. Treasuries were now close to those of Brazilian bonds and other Bradies. MinFins have for a long time been considered undervalued, compared to other emerging markets debt.
Tranche four rose the least following two strong selling orders, while tranche seven was the gain-leader, he said.
